title: Blackwell's trapdoor channel: certified capacity bounds 0.5749319 <= C <= 0.5749683
description:
In plain words. A box holds one ball. You drop a ball in, and one of the two balls inside falls out at random. How many bits per drop can a sender get across to someone watching the balls fall out? David Blackwell posed this in 1961 and it is still unsolved. The best proven interval we could find in print is 0.5 to 0.585. We pin the answer to 0.5749319 ≤ C ≤ 0.5749683 bits per drop, a gap of 0.0000363: about 2,300 times narrower than the best proven interval, and about 360 times narrower than the commonly quoted 0.572 to 0.585.

How. The floor is one explicit input recipe (the next ball depends on the lengths of the last three runs), whose information rate is computed with every rounding error bounded (Birch's bound, a backward recursion over all 2^24 output words, and a logarithm routine with a proven error bound). The ceiling is an order-15 output model checked with the duality bound of Huleihel, Sabag, Permuter, Kashyap and Shamai (2019) and its delayed-feedback form (2023), evaluated through a smaller equivalent dynamic program, with every logarithm enclosed and rounded upward and every Bellman residual checked exactly.

Checks. Ten sealed tests are listed with their verdicts, including two FAILED and one VOID, kept as they were scored. Hostile referee rounds on every proof, the paper and the package (internal lab checks, not external peer review). Independent second programs written from the definitions reproduce the ceiling to 15 decimals and the floor at depths 11 and 12; the full-depth floor rests on a refereed rounding-error proof and was re-run from a fresh copy of the package.

Not claimed. That either recipe is optimal, where C lies inside the interval, a closed form, any feedback capacity, or priority. Assumptions: correctly rounded IEEE 754 arithmetic, and Gallager's theorem for indecomposable channels (cited, not opened).

Prepared with AI assistance; what was checked, and by what, is stated above.
